intervals.note: Start: the review says the programme 'was proposed in 2004' and also that the collaboration 'started their program at LNGS in the late 1990s'; 2004 is used as a lower bound for the formal programme. End: last documented activity (2011).
intervals.quote: The WIMP Argon Programme (WARP) was proposed in 2004, emerging from R&D activities with liquid xenon and liquid argon for the ICARUS experiment.

intervals.quote: Though it never actually performed a physics run, a technical run was taken in 2011, to characterise the detector response.

name: WArP Collaboration
notes: No roster or member count was found; the Atlas records no memberships.
Host site Hall B is approximate: the papers place the prototype 'in the tunnel connecting HallA to HallB' and do not name a hall for the 100-litre detector.

summary.plain: The international team, mostly from Italian universities and INFN, with groups from Princeton and Krakow, that pioneered two-phase liquid argon detectors for WIMP dark matter at Gran Sasso with the WArP programme.
summary.technical: WARP Collaboration (affiliations on the 2008 first-results paper: Pavia, Naples, LNGS, Princeton, Krakow, L'Aquila, Padova). The programme grew out of ICARUS liquid argon R&D and was proposed in 2004 per a 2013 review; it started at LNGS in the late 1990s. No roster or member count was recorded.
